filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Identify real tuning surfaces in runtime VirtioFS and user-space SharedFS before implementing cache policy. Avoid attributing user-space view behavior to an unimplemented virtiofs device backend.
acceptance: Document supported cache controls and the layer owning each knob on every supported runtime version.
Profile stat, readdir, open and rename workloads across small and large trees with direct and cached mount paths.
Investigate full-tree scans and content hashing only where traces show material cost.
Any optimization must pass the file-sharing correctness/recovery suite and publish warm/cold results with stale-read failures counted.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: Mounted reverse Linux filesystem frontend not evidenced
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [FS-005] Design a mounted Linux filesystem view for macOS
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Add an actual Finder/shell-visible reverse filesystem for selected guest machines and volumes, with explicit frontend, permissions and coherence semantics.
acceptance: Select a supported macOS frontend and document its install, entitlement, trust and OS compatibility requirements.
Define stat/read/write/readdir/rename/xattr/locking behavior and authorization for each exposed guest root.
Verify Finder and shell workflows, concurrent mutation, disconnect/reconnect and offline error behavior with bounded caches.
Do not label existing copy operations or file-browser UI as a mounted reverse filesystem; gate rollout on the filesystem matrix.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: Path normalization exists; ownership mapping needs qualification
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [FS-006] Define path and ownership mapping across shared mounts
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Characterize current native mappings and design explicit per-share UID/GID behavior for shared distributions and managed host-account operation.
acceptance: Publish mapping rules for host paths, guest mount paths, UID/GID, supplementary groups and unsupported ownership changes.
Verify host-created and guest-created files retain the documented access and ownership behavior across restart.
Test chmod/chown, symlinks, paths outside the user home and paths denied to the dedicated runtime account.
Migration between mount modes cannot silently broaden host access or remap existing files to unintended users.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: Several write paths already exist; performance unqualified here
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [FS-007] Optimize measured bind-mount write bottlenecks
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Use profiles to improve the existing direct, SharedFS and overlay paths while preserving declared coherence and durability.
acceptance: Benchmark sequential, random, small-file and fsync-heavy workloads on equivalent data and mount configurations.
Attribute bottlenecks to hashing, copying, queueing, virtual filesystem or guest work before changing implementation.
Record flush latency, dirty-data behavior, host allocation and failure rates alongside throughput.
Optimizations pass crash/recovery and correctness checks and never compare nosync behavior to a durable competitor configuration without explicit separation.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: Mount strategies exist; validated policy contract incomplete
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [FS-008] Expose validated per-share cache policies
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Present existing direct, shared/per-container view and overlay choices as explicit policies only after their correctness and tuning controls are validated.
acceptance: Define safe defaults and document coherence, conflict and durability semantics for each supported policy.
Expose only controls supported by the selected engine and reject unavailable low-level VirtioFS options clearly.
Test mixed-policy mounts, policy changes, restart and cleanup without stale reads or unexpected host mutations.
Publish workload guidance based on measured results and keep correctness failures visible in benchmark reports.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: Ext4 base images and CoW storage already exist
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [STOR-001] Reconcile disk topology and allocation accounting
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Document existing per-VM ext4/base images and named-volume clones; decide separately whether a shared engine needs a single sparse data image.
acceptance: Publish storage ownership and layout for base images, VM writable disks, named volumes, clones and checkpoints.
Report logical capacity, allocated blocks and clone-shared extents without adding overlapping allocations as unique physical use.
Verify disk creation, insufficient-space handling, interrupted placement and cleanup on supported host filesystems.
Adopt a different shared-image topology only with capacity, performance, corruption-scope and migration evidence.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: Complete online resize path not found
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [STOR-002] Qualify safe disk expansion capabilities
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Investigate virtual block capacity changes and filesystem growth before committing to online expansion; provide a safe offline path when the backend cannot resize live.
acceptance: Document backend and guest support for live block capacity change and filesystem growth per runtime version.
Verify growth preserves file checksums, mounts and declared volume identity under active workloads.
Test host disk full, guest disk full, interruption and restart at each resize stage with recoverable state.
Unsupported online growth uses a clearly communicated safe offline procedure rather than silently risking attached disks.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: GC and allocation reporting exist; end-to-end discard unqualified
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [STOR-003] Validate end-to-end discard and host-space reclamation
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Trace guest filesystem discard through the virtual block backend to host sparse/APFS allocation and account correctly for shared clone extents.
acceptance: Measure host allocation before writes, after guest deletion and after discard for standalone and cloned disks.
Identify which filesystems, block backends and runtime versions actually release host storage.
Test active and stopped volumes, throttling, cancellation and concurrent clone/commit operations without corruption.
Expose reclaimed bytes and unsupported cases honestly; do not equate deleting guest files or cache entries with host disk reclamation.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: CoW clone and guarded promotion exist; portable backup absent
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [STOR-004] Add verifiable volume backup and restore
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Build portable, checksum-verified backup and restore above existing clone/commit primitives with explicit quiescence and application-consistency requirements.
acceptance: Define a versioned backup manifest containing volume identity, format, checksums, permissions and compatibility requirements.
Enforce the documented consistency policy and refuse unsafe live-writer snapshots unless an application-consistent mechanism is available.
Restore to a separate destination and verify checksums before replacing any existing volume.
Exercise interrupted export/import, corrupt archives, insufficient space and cross-version restore with the original data preserved on failure.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: Disk checkpoints exist; full VM-state snapshots absent
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [STOR-005] Define and harden checkpoint and snapshot semantics
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Differentiate existing disk checkpoints from memory/device-state snapshots and decide which product guarantee is required before implementation.
acceptance: Document whether each snapshot captures disk only, application-consistent state or complete VM memory/device state.
Harden disk and metadata publication/recovery so interruption cannot silently select mismatched checkpoint components.
Verify checkpoint clone, restore, deletion, version compatibility and rollback with data checksums.
Any full VM-state mode requires confirmed public framework support and physical validation; unsupported cases retain disk-only semantics.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: vmnet, native network and subnet allocation implemented
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [NET-001] Qualify the existing network and resolver baseline
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Extend the current vmnet/native paths and deterministic shim subnet allocator with an engine-specific reliability matrix rather than adding a bootstrap stack by default.
acceptance: Verify outbound TCP, UDP, DNS, IPv4 and supported IPv6 behavior for every supported engine and network mode.
Test VPN and split DNS transitions, sleep/wake, MTU changes, host subnet collisions and runtime restart.
Exercise repeated network allocation and ambiguous teardown without reusing resources whose cleanup is unconfirmed.
Publish supported direct-IP, host-only and isolation behavior and retain raw failures and environment metadata in network benchmarks.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: Published ports exist; sandbox UDP/IPv6 bind gaps
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [NET-002] Complete port-forwarding parity and lifecycle behavior
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Extend existing native published ports and sandbox TCP relays, explicitly resolving differing bind defaults and unsupported sandbox protocols.
acceptance: Document and test default bind scope and explicit loopback, IPv4 and supported IPv6 addresses across engines.
Add or explicitly capability-gate sandbox UDP and IPv6 forwarding with protocol-specific correctness tests.
Verify port conflicts, thousands of connection churn operations, backpressure, half-close and cancellation without leaks.
Test sleep/restart rebind and distinguish explicitly published Docker ports from any future automatic discovery of guest listeners.

filed_issue_dispositions.status: Sandbox host.micropod.internal alias exists
filed_issue_dispositions.title: [NET-003] Standardize host gateway names across engines
filed_issue_dispositions.scope: Reuse the existing sandbox alias and define supported host-access semantics for Apple, sandbox, external Docker and optional shared-kernel modes.
acceptance: Publish the stable supported host name and address behavior per engine and network mode.
Verify resolution and reachability under IPv4, supported IPv6, VPN transitions and host-only networks.
Ensure disabled networking or denied host access cannot be bypassed by selecting the gateway alias.
Test restart and network replacement without stale aliases, and document when an external Docker engine retains its own host-name conventions.
